sentences.text: The genus Zby contains only one known species, Zby atlanticus.
This animal is estimated to have been between 15 and 18 meters long.
Zby is distinguished from other sauropods by four unique features, including a prominent ridge on the humerus near the deltopectoral crest.
The fossils of Zby were discovered in 1996 in the Lourinhã Formation of Portugal by Octávio Mateus.
Zby was first described and named by Octávio Mateus, Philip D. Mannion, and Paul Upchurch in 2014.
Most anatomical features indicate that Zby was a non-neosauropod eusauropod belonging to the Turiasauria group.
Researchers suggest that Zby is closely related to Turiasaurus riodevensis from contemporaneous deposits in eastern Spain.
Zby is classified within the unranked family Turiasauria.
Zby lived during the late Jurassic period, between 155 and 150 million years ago in the Kimmeridgian stage.
The time range for Zby is the Kimmeridgian stage, from 152.21 to 149.2 million years ago.
It is noted that Zby was initially thought to be the species Turiasaurus riodevensis before being reclassified.
